objects.description: Enumeration of music sequence identifiers used by the sound system. Values map to different background tracks and jingles. Starts at -1 for unknown and lists many course/flow-specific tracks, ending with MUSIC_SEQ_MAX sentinel.
Scoped enum describing which button a dialog returned (cancel/ok/yes/no/abort/retry/ignore). Returned by pfd::message::result().
Scoped enum selecting which set of buttons a message dialog should display.
Scoped enum selecting the icon style used by dialogs/notifications.
Bitflag options controlling file/folder dialogs (multiselect, overwrite behavior, forcing initial path). Bitwise operators are provided for combining/testing flags.

Configuration/state class for portable-file-dialogs. Manages backend availability, verbosity, and rescanning helpers. Users can toggle verbosity and query availability. Internals track platform helper flags.
Internal async process/task runner used to launch platform dialogs or functions and collect results, with cancellation support.
Internal platform helpers. On Windows provides RAII wrappers for DLL loading, OLE initialization, and activation context for themed dialogs.
Base class for dialogs providing backend selection, quoting utilities, and an async executor handle. Not intended for direct use by clients.
Abstracted file/folder dialog base providing constructors and result helpers. Used by open_file, save_file, and select_folder.
Utility providing platform-specific path helpers (home directory and path separator).
Transient notification popup class. Constructs and shows a desktop notification with optional icon.
Modal message dialog with configurable buttons and icon. Use result() to map the user’s choice to pfd::button.
Concrete file-open dialog widget. Supports multiselect via pfd::opt::multiselect or deprecated ctor flag.
Concrete file-save dialog widget with overwrite control via pfd::opt::force_overwrite or deprecated ctor flag.
Concrete folder selection dialog widget. Returns the chosen directory path.

functions.name: GameEngine_OTRSigCheck
functions.description: Checks whether the provided byte sequence/string begins with a known OTR signature. Used by LOAD_ASSET to decide whether a path refers to an embedded resource (signature present) or a plain path. Exact matching rules and signature format are not documented here.
requirements: imgData should point to a valid, readable, null-terminated C string or memory buffer large enough for the signature check (exact length unknown).
Returns true if the signature is recognized, false otherwise.
Behavior and required format of the signature are unknown from this header.

functions.name: pfd::operator<<
functions.signature: std::ostream& pfd::operator<<(std::ostream& s, std::vector<std::string> const& v);
functions.description: Stream insertion operator to print a vector of strings, separating elements with a single space. Primarily used for debugging command lines built for desktop helpers.
requirements: s must be a valid output stream; on failure states, no output may be produced.
v may contain arbitrary strings; no quoting or escaping is performed, so elements containing spaces will be emitted as-is.

functions.name: pfd::settings::available
functions.description: Returns whether portable-file-dialogs can show dialogs on the current platform/configuration. Always true on Windows and macOS; on Linux/Unix returns true if a supported helper (zenity, matedialog, qarma, or kdialog) is found; currently false on Emscripten.
requirements: No object instance required (static).
Call to check runtime availability before constructing dialogs, especially on non-Windows platforms.

functions.name: pfd::settings::verbose
functions.description: Globally enables or disables verbose logging of the backend commands used by portable-file-dialogs.
requirements: No object instance required (static).
Setting affects subsequent dialog operations process-wide.

functions.name: pfd::settings::rescan
functions.description: Forces a rescan of installed desktop helpers (zenity, kdialog, etc.), refreshing internal availability flags.
requirements: No object instance required (static).
Use when the environment changes at runtime (e.g., helper installed) and you need to refresh detection.

functions.name: pfd::path::home
functions.description: Returns the current user’s home directory as a platform-appropriate absolute path. Uses platform-specific mechanisms to locate it; falls back to "/" on failure.
requirements: No object instance required (static).
Returned string may be empty or "/" if detection fails; callers should handle that case.

functions.name: pfd::path::separator
functions.description: Returns the native path separator for the current platform: "\\" on Windows, "/" elsewhere.
requirements: No object instance required (static).

functions.name: pfd::notify::notify
functions.signature: pfd::notify::notify(std::string const& title, std::string const& message, pfd::icon _icon = pfd::icon::info);
functions.description: Displays a transient desktop notification with a title, message, and optional icon. On Windows uses shell notifications; on macOS/Linux uses desktop helpers (osascript/zenity/kdialog). Icon ‘question’ is mapped to ‘info’.
requirements: Desktop notification support must be available (see pfd::settings::available), otherwise a helper command will still be attempted and may fail silently.
title and message should be UTF-8 strings; very long texts may be truncated by the underlying system.
On Emscripten, functionality is stubbed (FIXME in code); do not rely on visible notifications there.

functions.name: pfd::message::message
functions.signature: pfd::message::message(std::string const& title, std::string const& text, pfd::choice _choice = pfd::choice::ok_cancel, pfd::icon _icon = pfd::icon::info);
functions.description: Opens a modal message dialog with specified text, title, button layout (choice), and icon. Uses native APIs on Windows and desktop helpers on other platforms.
requirements: Dialog availability should be checked with pfd::settings::available on non-Windows platforms.
title and text should be UTF-8 strings.
On Emscripten, only alert/confirm is emulated; only ok or ok_cancel behaviors are supported there.

functions.name: pfd::message::result
functions.description: Blocks until the message dialog is closed and returns which button was pressed, mapped to pfd::button values. Falls back to ok/cancel when exact mapping is unknown.
requirements: Must be called after constructing pfd::message to retrieve user selection.
May block until the user interacts with the dialog or it is programmatically closed.
On some backends, mappings may be inferred from exit codes and output; unexpected codes map to ok for 0, cancel otherwise.

functions.name: pfd::open_file::open_file
functions.signature: pfd::open_file::open_file(std::string const& title, std::string const& default_path = "", std::vector<std::string> const& filters = { "All Files", "*" }, pfd::opt options = pfd::opt::none);
functions.description: Constructs an asynchronous file open dialog. Supports optional default path, file type filters, and options (e.g., multiselect).
requirements: On non-Windows platforms, a supported desktop helper must be available (see pfd::settings::available).
filters should be an even-length list of pairs: display name, pattern (e.g., {"Images","*.png *.jpg"}).
default_path may be a directory or file path; if a directory, it is used as initial directory.
Use pfd::opt::multiselect to allow multiple selection.

functions.name: pfd::open_file::result
functions.description: Returns the selected file paths. Blocks until the dialog completes. In multiselect mode returns all selected paths; otherwise typically returns one or zero entries.
requirements: Call after constructing pfd::open_file; may block until user completes interaction.
Returned vector may be empty if the user cancels.

functions.name: pfd::save_file::save_file
functions.signature: pfd::save_file::save_file(std::string const& title, std::string const& default_path = "", std::vector<std::string> const& filters = { "All Files", "*" }, pfd::opt options = pfd::opt::none);
functions.description: Constructs an asynchronous file save dialog with optional default path, filters, and options. By default, prompts on overwrite unless pfd::opt::force_overwrite is set.
requirements: On non-Windows platforms, a supported desktop helper must be available (see pfd::settings::available).
filters should be an even-length list of pairs: display name, pattern.
default_path can include a suggested filename or directory.
To disable overwrite confirmation, pass pfd::opt::force_overwrite.

functions.name: pfd::save_file::result
functions.description: Returns the chosen save path as a string. Blocks until the dialog completes. Returns an empty string on cancel.
requirements: Call after constructing pfd::save_file; may block until user completes interaction.
Returned string may be empty if the user cancels.

functions.name: pfd::select_folder::select_folder
functions.signature: pfd::select_folder::select_folder(std::string const& title, std::string const& default_path = "", pfd::opt options = pfd::opt::none);
functions.description: Constructs a folder selection dialog. Optionally sets a default path; on supported systems, can force the dialog to use the provided path.
requirements: On non-Windows platforms, a supported desktop helper must be available (see pfd::settings::available).
default_path should be an existing directory for best results.
options may include pfd::opt::force_path (used on some backends).

functions.name: pfd::select_folder::result
functions.description: Returns the selected directory path as a string. Blocks until the dialog completes. Returns an empty string on cancel.
requirements: Call after constructing pfd::select_folder; may block until user completes interaction.
Returned string may be empty if the user cancels.

endpoints.name: pfd::operator<<
pfd::settings::available
pfd::settings::verbose
pfd::settings::rescan
pfd::path::home
pfd::path::separator

unharnessable_functions.name: pfd::notify::notify
unharnessable_functions.reason: Constructing UI notifications may spawn OS dialogs and side-effect external processes, risking blocking in a headless fuzzer.

unharnessable_functions.name: pfd::message::message
unharnessable_functions.reason: Creating modal UI dialogs can trigger user-visible windows and potential hangs in non-interactive fuzzing environments.

unharnessable_functions.name: pfd::message::result
unharnessable_functions.reason: Retrieving the result from a modal dialog may block waiting for user interaction, unsuitable for fuzzing.

unharnessable_functions.name: pfd::open_file::open_file
unharnessable_functions.reason: Constructing a file-open dialog may launch external GUI helpers, which is unsafe and potentially blocking for a fuzzer.

unharnessable_functions.name: pfd::open_file::result
unharnessable_functions.reason: Waiting for file dialog results can block indefinitely for user input, not suitable for fuzzing.

unharnessable_functions.name: pfd::save_file::save_file
unharnessable_functions.reason: Constructing a file-save dialog may invoke GUI helpers and side-effect the environment, risking blocking in fuzzing.

unharnessable_functions.name: pfd::save_file::result
unharnessable_functions.reason: Waiting for save dialog results can block for user interaction, incompatible with automated fuzzing.

unharnessable_functions.name: pfd::select_folder::select_folder
unharnessable_functions.reason: Constructing a folder selection dialog may open GUI windows/helpers, which is unsafe in headless fuzzing.

unharnessable_functions.name: pfd::select_folder::result
unharnessable_functions.reason: Retrieving the selected folder blocks awaiting user interaction, unsuitable for fuzzing.

unharnessable_functions.name: GameEngine_OTRSigCheck
unharnessable_functions.reason: The symbol is not linked in this build, causing an undefined reference at link time so it cannot be exercised.

data_types.description: An unconstrained byte string treated as generic UTF-8/bytes. May contain any characters including spaces, quotes, NULs (if allowed by std::string), and non-printable bytes. No specific format or encoding is required or interpreted by the target function.

generators.generator:
import random
import struct
from typing import List

# Target: Generate interesting arbitrary strings for pfd::operator<< fuzzer stub.
# The stub pulls:
# - an unsigned int selector (bitmask deciding how many strings to include, up to 3)
# - up to three FUZZ_PARAM_STR() strings
# Our goal: return a single bytes buffer that the fuzz harness will slice into
# these values deterministically. We will encode:
# [u32 selector][len1][str1][len2][str2][len3][str3]
# where each len is u16 length of following bytes, present even if selector bit is 0
# (harness typically just requests values sequentially; keeping consistent layout ensures
# deterministic extraction regardless of which bits are used). Strings can contain spaces,
# quotes, UTF-8, and edge-case content to exercise printing/spacing behavior without being malformed.

MAX_TOTAL = 4096

EDGE_STRINGS = [
    b"",  # empty element
    b" ",  # single space
    b"multiple   spaces",
    b"leading space",
    b"trailing space ",
    b"tabs\tand\nnewlines",
    b"quotes ' \" backslash \\",
    "emoji \U0001F600 \U0001F680".encode("utf-8"),
    "latin-1 \u00E9\u00F1".encode("utf-8"),
    b"* ? [ ] ( ) { } | ^ $ . +",
    b"path/like/with/slashes",
    b"C:\\path\\with\\backslashes",
    b"--flags --option=value",
    b"name with spaces.txt",
    b"*.png *.jpg",
]


def _rand_str(rng: random.Random) -> bytes:
    choice = rng.randrange(5)
    if choice == 0:
        # Pick from curated edge cases
        return rng.choice(EDGE_STRINGS)
    elif choice == 1:
        # ASCII printable with spaces
        length = rng.randint(1, 128)
        alphabet = b"abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyzABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZ0123456789 _-.,:/\\'\"[](){}*?+$^|"
        return bytes(rng.choice(alphabet) for _ in range(length))
    elif choice == 2:
        # UTF-8 mix including multi-byte
        chunks: List[bytes] = []
        for _ in range(rng.randint(1, 10)):
            t = rng.randrange(4)
            if t == 0:
                chunks.append(rng.choice(EDGE_STRINGS))
            elif t == 1:
                # random ascii word
                wl = rng.randint(1, 12)
                chunks.append(bytes(rng.choice(b"abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz") for _ in range(wl)))
            elif t == 2:
                # unicode emoji range
                cp = rng.randrange(0x1F300, 0x1FAFF)
                try:
                    chunks.append(chr(cp).encode("utf-8"))
                except Exception:
                    pass
            else:
                # accented latin
                cp = rng.choice([0x00E9, 0x00F1, 0x00FC, 0x010D, 0x0159])
                chunks.append(chr(cp).encode("utf-8"))
        s = b" ".join(chunks)
        return s[:512]
    elif choice == 3:
        # Repeated pattern to test spacing behavior when concatenated
        token = rng.choice([b"foo", b"bar", b"baz", b"qux", b"--", b"*"])
        reps = rng.randint(1, 50)
        sep = rng.choice([b" ", b"", b"  ", b"\t"])  # different whitespace
        s = sep.join([token] * reps)
        return s[:512]
    else:
        # Filter-like string that includes spaces to simulate command segments
        labels = [b"All Files", b"Images", b"Text Files", b"C++", b"Markdown"]
        pats = [b"*", b"*.png *.jpg", b"*.txt", b"*.cpp *.hpp", b"*.md"]
        return rng.choice(labels) + b" " + rng.choice(pats)


def _pack_len_prefixed(b: bytes) -> bytes:
    # Length as uint16, truncated to 1024 to keep total under limit
    b = b[:1024]
    return struct.pack("<H", len(b)) + b


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)

    # Decide selector bits to vary vector size and emptiness; also include combinations
    patterns = [0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7]
    selector = rng.choice(patterns)

    # Build three strings regardless of selector; harness will consume sequentially
    s1 = _rand_str(rng)
    s2 = _rand_str(rng)
    s3 = _rand_str(rng)

    # Assemble buffer
    buf = struct.pack("<I", selector)
    buf += _pack_len_prefixed(s1)
    buf += _pack_len_prefixed(s2)
    buf += _pack_len_prefixed(s3)

    # Ensure size cap
    return buf[:MAX_TOTAL]
